status_summary: Executive Order 14164 (2025-01-20) and Bondi's 2025-02-05 memo lifted the federal execution moratorium and directed prosecutors to seek death in specified categories, including murders of law enforcement officers and capital crimes by people in the country illegally. On 2026-04-24 DOJ announced it had authorized seeking death against 44 defendants, readopted the pentobarbital protocol, directed the Bureau of Prisons to add other execution methods including the firing squad, and planned rules on habeas review and clemency petitions. President Biden had commuted 37 of 40 federal death sentences in December 2024, so the death row population the Mandate described no longer exists, and no federal execution since January 2021 was found in the sources reviewed.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14164, Restoring the Death Penalty and Protecting Public Safety, signed (Federal Register 2025-01-30): directs the Attorney General to pursue capital punishment, seek death in specified cases, assist states with execution drugs, and seek reversal of precedents limiting capital punishment.

Bondi memo lifts the 2021 execution moratorium, directs prosecutors to seek death for the most serious provable offenses, orders review of earlier no-seek decisions within 120 days, and directs the Office of Legal Policy to assess readopting the single-drug pentobarbital protocol.

DOJ announces it has authorized seeking death against 44 defendants (nine personally by Acting AG Blanche), readopted the pentobarbital protocol, directed the Bureau of Prisons to expand methods (including the firing squad) and examine facility changes, and prepared a legislative proposal, with rulemaking on habeas and clemency to follow.

title: Enforce the federal death penalty and seek finality for capital cases
uncertainties: Checked 2026-10-13: the Bureau of Prisons federal executions history page lists no execution after 2021-01-16, which replaces the earlier Wikipedia-based basis for the no-execution statement (the page's own update date is not shown, so a very recent execution could be missed). The DOJ press release of 2026-04-24 (number 26-400) was re-read and mentions no execution dates; it says a proposed rule on capital clemency petitions and a possible habeas rule were planned within weeks, but a Federal Register query for Justice Department documents on the death penalty, executions or capital habeas after 2026-04-24 returned none, so neither rule was found published. Three web searches found no execution date, court ruling on the protocol or later DOJ announcement beyond the April coverage; absence from search results is not proof that none exists. Death-notice counts after April 2026 and the Mandate's child sexual abuse item were not checked.
